newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES LITTLE CHANGED AFTER TENDER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES LITTLE CHANGED AFTER TENDER.

text.p: Short term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted little changed on Friday despite a substantial fall in the treasury bill rate at Thursday's weekly auction, dealers said.
They said most market players felt the treasury bill rate, a direction pointer for other rates, had come down too drastically at the tender.
"We think one institution must have made a mistake on its tender price and the Reserve Bank takes the lowest price, hence the fall in the TB (treasury bill) rate," one dealer said.

"But other rates have not come down substantially in line with the treasury bill rate and people are generally keeping a low profile on the market. No one is keen to sell at this point in time," he added.

On Friday the buying rate for treasury bills was down at 15.44 percent from last week's 19.36 and a few discount houses were selling some of their old stock of the central bank paper at 15.50 percent.
The indicative buying rate for NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days was unchanged at 20 percent while bankers acceptances eased slightly to 19.25 from 19.50 percent.
Call money however tumbled to a zero to 15 percentage range from 18 percent in a market which opened with an unsettled surplus of Z$943.6 million.
